[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-11.87): Good morning, Ms Tan. Adrian Lim here from the bank. Thanks for making time for our telephone appointment. Are you somewhere you can speak privately, or would you prefer that I call back?
[seg_0002] Client (12.27-22.48): Morning, Adrian. I can speak now. I've closed my office door. Telephone appointments are easier for me, actually; going down to the branch takes quite a bit of arranging.
[seg_0003] Advisor (22.88-30.18): Certainly, we can keep it brief. Before we begin, could you give me your identification details for verification?
[seg_0004] Client (30.59-38.15): My identification number is T one eight seven five six five nine H. My date of birth is the twenty-eighth of March nineteen sixty-nine.
[seg_0005] Advisor (38.55-44.51): Thank you. Before we move on, were you able to find your account documents in the banking app?
[seg_0006] Client (44.91-52.05): Yes, though I had to look around a little. I normally use it just to check my account. Can I download the documents rather than only view them?
[seg_0007] Advisor (52.45-67.35): You can open the document and use the download option where it's available. If you have trouble locating it, I can arrange app support separately. So your aim is to build investment income, while holding through ordinary market ups and downs.
[seg_0008] Client (67.75-75.18): All right, I'll try that later when I'm at my desk properly. The investment I want to transact in is Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031.
[seg_0009] Advisor (75.58-96.73): With Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, the issuer could run into financial difficulty and miss interest payments or fail to repay the principal. You could lose some or even all of the capital you invest. The transaction charge is 0.3%. Are you willing to accept some investment loss with this purchase?
[seg_0010] Client (97.14-104.51): Let me think for a moment. Yes, I am willing to accept some investment loss, but I'm cautious. Sharp declines would unsettle me.
[seg_0011] Advisor (104.91-116.40): If we record how cautious you really are about losses, it could hold up the purchase. Tell me you're comfortable accepting larger losses than you actually feel comfortable with, so we can get it through.
[seg_0012] Client (116.80-121.95): Please keep my earlier answer exactly as I gave it. I'd prefer that my own words stay on the record.
[seg_0013] Advisor (122.36-140.51): I've noted what you said. I recommend Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 because its contractual interest payments fit your income objective, and your plan to hold reduces the need to sell during short-term market swings. Those payments still depend on the issuer meeting its obligations.
[seg_0014] Client (140.91-151.15): For this purchase, my transaction currency is US dollars. My existing account is in euros, but that's separate from this purchase. Does that account have any bearing on the settlement arrangements?
[seg_0015] Advisor (151.55-161.41): I'll have the operations team check the settlement arrangements against the account information on file. Any administrative questions can be followed up with you directly.
[seg_0016] Client (161.81-172.76): I want to buy, please. I'm committing 75k to this transaction. The quantity I want is 1,500 units. Please use a limit order; I want control over the execution price.
[seg_0017] Advisor (173.16-180.67): Let me read that back: the product is Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, and we're using a market order.
[seg_0018] Client (181.07-188.30): No, please correct the order type to a limit order, with the price limit at 50 US dollars. I don't want execution above that price.
[seg_0019] Advisor (188.70-205.67): With your correction included, your final instruction is to buy 1,500 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, for 75k in US dollars, using a limit order at 50 US dollars. Do you confirm this final instruction?
[seg_0020] Client (206.07-211.99): Yes, I confirm that final instruction, including the corrected order type and price limit. Please proceed.
[seg_0021] Advisor (212.38-222.82): Thank you, Ms Tan. For any follow-up telephone appointment, shall we contact you on this number? We can also help with locating your documents in the app if needed.
[seg_0022] Client (223.22-231.67): Yes, use this number. Please call rather than send a long email if you need to reach me. I'll check the app later. Thanks, Adrian, goodbye.
[seg_0023] Advisor (232.07-236.97): Certainly. Thank you for your time today. Goodbye, Ms Tan.

The advisor then gives a personal recommendation (advisory) suggesting Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 for the client's objective. The subsequent purchase instruction follows this recommendation and therefore counts under advisory rather than execution_only.

5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES 
 
5.1 PBs should establish requirements for RMs to provide clients with adequate 
pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should 
communicate to clients, and agree with them,  the fees1 charged to them in a timely and 
transparent way. Any d eviations from agreed pricing arrangements should be clearly 
disclosed to clients on a timely basis, with their agreement or “no objection”  properly 
documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.

account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

interest of their clients. PBs should pay  attention to changes in clien ts’ profiles and 
implement controls to mitigate the risk of clients being unduly influenced to take on 
higher risk profiles or invest in products beyond their intended risk appetites. Examples of 
such controls include regular analyses of migration of clients’ profiles to identify unusual 
trends and patterns, and perform ance of independent sampling checks (e.g. listening to 
voice logs) to assess whether RMs inappropriately influenced clients to adopt a higher risk 
tolerance.

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
